title: He worked with his hands… so no one could question his heart.
paragraphs: He worked with his hands… so no one could question his heart.
The apostle Paul the Apostle—a preacher carrying eternity in his mouth—still chose to carry leather, tools, and sweat in his hands.
Not because ministry wasn’t worthy of support.
“I have not coveted anyone’s silver or gold or clothing.” — Acts 20:33
“You yourselves know that these hands of mine have supplied my own needs…” — Acts 20:34
Paul wasn’t saying ministers shouldn’t be supported.
In fact, he clearly taught the opposite:
“The Lord has commanded that those who preach the gospel should receive their living from the gospel.” — 1 Corinthians 9:14
So why did he refuse it sometimes?

He would rather suffer loss…
than let anyone mistake the Gospel for a business.

Because today, it’s easy to mix calling with comfort…
anointing with ambition…
ministry with money.
“I won’t let silver compete with souls.”
And that’s where grace walks in.
Because this isn’t about condemning provision.

And the Gospel is still free—
even if it costs us everything to carry it.
“Would I still serve… if no one paid me?”
Because in Christ, we don’t serve for gain.
We serve because we’ve already been given everything.
We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
